items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Linden Mills the trumpeter we called Link, took Timmie up town.

ctx.x: Benny brought the fellow into the room and introduced him to us. His name was Baron Timothy Rosenkranktz and he was from Denmark. We later found out that he was a jazz fan and knew a lot about some of the big swing bands and the musicians. But Benny's was the first negro band he had heard in New York because he had only been in the city a couple of days when he learned that Benny had a band at the Empire ballroom. Timmie (as he was later to become known) had come to the ballroom in full dress because that was the…

The next night he was back again but dressed like an ordinary human being! When we finished the night Timmie wanted to go up to Harlem, so Linden Mills the trumpeter we called Link, took Timmie up town. Link smoked reefers and he was the one who introduced the stuff to Timmie who became so fascinated with Harlem that he finally moved there.

For some unknown reason, Benny began to lose interest in the band and Bill Dillard left to join Teddy Hill who had been the tenor man with Luis Russell at one time and now had his own band at the Savoy. Two weeks before the time for us to finish at the Empire, Benny told us that he would be disbanding.
